result: The hot-text tracer answers every library time read (rdtsc, vDSO clock_gettime/gettimeofday/time, their syscall fallbacks) from a virtual clock; regen.sh fails a build whose mktime trace changes when slowed 2 s per time read. Signatures and layout-bins byte-identical across two mei builds, a 2 s-slowed mei build and a keke build.

gate.affected: clippy, static, direct tier green (trace-time-pin-gate, before xtask test); xtask test and full-profile hot_text_products pending in that job

rulings.item: NUMA topology is a host input of the trace: keke/mei allow 2 nodes, shiki/kanon 1, so the heap's node reads (rseq, vDSO getcpu) are traced on some build hosts only
rulings.recommendation: follow-up story: a virtual 2-node topology pinned to node 0 in the tracer (get_mempolicy answer plus the node read), chosen by measuring hot_text_products on a 2-node and a 1-node host

informational: regen.sh's slowed-trace check covers the mktime mode only and catches a host clock only together with a host TSC (the TSC gate shields later clock reads): plants tpin-tsc-host and tpin-vdso-clock-host are equivalent for that trace, measured SURVIVED in plants-1
RLIMIT_AS of the build's caller reaches the traced programs (heap registry sizing); unlimited on the build hosts, not changed

impact.what: trace-at-build layout no longer depends on how long the trace took (the mktime recheck that moved compare to bin 1 on a slow keke build)
build-time check (regen.sh slowed mktime trace) and 3 plants
one extra parallel gdb trace per build (page_faults mktime, about 2 s sleep per time read per CPU class)

improvement: Remote commands that start a job must not chain anything before setsid: one of mine did and held the ssh until the harness timed out; a jobrun-start wrapper script would stop this happening.
next_step: Read trace-time-pin-gate (xtask test, full-profile hot_text_products) and trace-time-pin-plants2; then the NUMA ruling.
